one_liner: CLI wrapper around clangd that reports clang-tidy diagnostics much faster than standalone clang-tidy.
what_it_does: clangd-tidy runs clangd in the background as an LSP server and collects its clang-tidy diagnostics, then prints them in a clang-tidy-like CLI format. It is designed as a drop-in replacement for the clang-tidy command in build systems and CI scripts, taking the same kind of file list and a compile_commands.json. It also adds a diff-mode tool (clangd-tidy-diff) that lints only changed lines, plus optional clang-format checking and GitHub Actions annotations.
how_it_is_fast: Standalone clang-tidy parses and checks the full AST of every included header for every translation unit, even though it suppresses warnings from headers by default. clangd instead builds and caches an AST scoped to what a file actually needs, the same incremental analysis it uses for live editor diagnostics, so clangd-tidy inherits that lighter-weight AST construction instead of clang-tidy's from-scratch per-file header checking. No other technique (caching, parallel dispatch beyond clangd's own worker pool, etc.) is described in the README or source.
when_to_use: Running clang-tidy-style checks in CI on a C/C++ codebase where wall-clock time matters
You already have clangd installed/configured and a working compile_commands.json
You want per-file grouped diagnostics instead of clang-tidy's duplicated per-header warnings
You want incremental linting of only changed lines via clangd-tidy-diff (e.g. gradual rollout of checks on a legacy codebase)
You also want code-formatting checks (clang-format) folded into the same CI step (-f/--format)
when_not_to_use: You need --fix / automatic fixups; clangd-tidy has no fix-application support, only editor code actions
You rely on clang-tidy checks that clangd's TidyProvider doesn't support; those are silently dropped, not reported as skipped
Exact diagnostic parity with clang-tidy matters (there are open, acknowledged behavioral discrepancies, e.g. issues #7, #15, #16)
You can't install/configure clangd in your CI image, or don't have a compile_commands.json
You want a large, heavily-used, battle-tested tool; this is a small single-maintainer project (161 stars)

integration.dependencies: clangd (external binary); Python 3.8+; attrs, cattrs, typing-extensions (auto-installed via pip); tqdm optional for progress bar
integration.min_toolchain: Python 3.8+; a clangd binary (version affects available .clangd diagnostics config, e.g. UnusedIncludes needs clangd-14+, MissingIncludes needs clangd-17+)
integration.platforms: POSIX (per PyPI classifiers: Operating System :: POSIX); no Windows classifier listed
integration.thread_safety: not documented (single Python CLI process driving one clangd subprocess over LSP; -j controls clangd's internal async worker/background-index thread count, not multiple clangd-tidy processes)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same CLI shape (pass filenames, -p for compile_commands.json dir) but no --fix, and it silently disables clang-tidy checks clangd doesn't support, so output isn't a strict superset/match of clang-tidy's

gotchas: Silently disables clang-tidy checks unsupported by clangd's TidyProvider (listed in LLVM's TidyProvider.cpp) rather than erroring or warning
No --fix option; the README suggests using editor code actions instead since the tool targets CI, not local fix workflows
Known behavioral discrepancies vs clang-tidy are tracked as open issues (#7, #15, #16), not resolved
Default -j (clangd async workers) is 1, so out-of-the-box throughput depends on tuning -j for parallelism
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Not directly comparable to the other sibling entries (Biome, Oxlint, Pyrefly, ty, Ruff), which target JS/TS or Python; clangd-tidy is the only C/C++ formatter-linter-LSP entry in this category so far, so 'no siblings catalogued yet' for its actual competitor set (clang-tidy variants).
verified_claims_summary: The README's 'Comparison with clang-tidy' section states clangd-tidy is 'significantly faster than clang-tidy (over 10x in my experience)' when running the same checks over a codebase, because clangd only builds an AST from included headers where clang-tidy checks all headers. No benchmark script, target codebase, compiler flags, or hardware are given — it's the author's stated personal experience, not a reproducible measurement.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-02-09) and MIT-licensed, but a small, single-maintainer project (161 stars) — usability tagged 'copyable' rather than a heavyweight dependency.
